ENGINEERING GUIDE

Planning MES / ERP Integration for an Anodizing Line

Define data ownership, interfaces and acceptance checks before connecting an anodizing line to factory management software.

PROJECT PLANNING / DAIMENG TECHNOLOGY

A network connection is only one part of integration. The important work is agreeing what each system knows, what it controls and what happens when information is missing.

Start with the production workflow

Map how an order becomes a production batch, how the batch is identified and how completion is reported. Identify the people who resolve exceptions. Use this workflow to decide which information needs to move between the line and factory management software.

Define a shared data dictionary

Document identifiers, units, timestamps and allowed values. A profile code or recipe name is useful only if both sides interpret it consistently. Decide which system owns each record and how changes are approved.

Agree the integration boundary

Daimeng’s published control system information describes interfaces for factory management systems, including MES and ERP. Discuss the exact data, connection method and responsibilities with the engineering and IT teams before finalizing a project.

Plan for interrupted connections

Specify how operators see a missing connection, what production can continue and how records are reconciled afterwards. Discuss duplicate records, incomplete messages and changes received during production.

Test the real scenarios

Include a normal batch, a revised order, an unavailable connection and a restart in acceptance planning. Define success in operational terms: the right information arrives once, the operator understands the state, and the systems agree on the result.

Integration scope and network design should be approved by the people responsible for both systems.
